title: Societal infrastructure in the age of Artificial General Intelligence
problem: Generative AI services are placing unprecedented compute demands on existing computing infrastructure, while traditional architectural patterns for efficiency improvements have stalled and can no longer provide sufficient gains.
motivation: Computing infrastructure must be fundamentally redesigned to efficiently support generative AI workloads while meeting security and sustainability requirements.
method: The paper proposes building AI infrastructure by coupling hardware and software design across all layers—networks, accelerators (specialized chips for AI), and servers—rather than trying to squeeze more speed out of general-purpose computers. Each infrastructure piece is optimized specifically for AI algorithm demands through co-design, where hardware and software are developed together so they work perfectly with each other. Security and sustainability are integrated into this approach from the start.
key_novelty: Instead of making general-purpose computers faster, the strategy is to design AI hardware and software together as optimized pairs, each tailored to work specifically with the other.
contributions: Analysis of efficiency plateau in traditional computing architectures for AI workloads
Framework for specialized hardware-software co-optimization across infrastructure layers
Concrete examples of specialized infrastructure designs from Google
Integration of security and sustainability as fundamental design constraints
limitations: Not discussed - this is a position/vision paper without specific technical evaluation or experimental results.
